en.title: Minister Shahid holds a telephone call with the new Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka
en.description: Minister Shahid holds a telephone call with the new Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka
en.body:
Minister Shahid holds a telephone call with the new Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid held a telephone call with the new Minister of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka, Professor Gamini Lakshman Peiris, today.

During the telephone call, Minister Shahid warmly congratulated Minister Peiris on his appointment as the new Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka.

The two Ministers reflected on the close historical relationship between Maldives and Sri Lanka. The Ministers also shared views on key issues such as climate change, peace and security and sustainable development, and explored new avenues to further strengthen the ties between Maldives and Sri Lanka.

The Ministers spoke on the current Covid-19 situation in their respective countries, and expressed their concerns with regard to the situation of the countries in South Asia. The Ministers also discussed the measures being implemented to contain the spread of the pandemic and the importance of vaccination.

Thanking the Government of Sri Lanka for their support to his candidature as President of the 76th session of the UN General Assembly, Minister Shahid gave his assurance to continue to work closely with Sri Lanka at the UN to realize his vision for the Presidency of Hope, and other international fora.

Minister Shahid and Minister Peiris reaffirmed their commitment to further enhance and strengthen the cooperation between Maldives and Sri Lanka bilaterally and in the multilateral sphere.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends a congratulatory message to the New Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka
en.description: Minister Shahid sends a congratulatory message to the New Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends a congratulatory message to the New Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a congratulatory message to Professor Gamini Lakshman Peiris on his appointment as the new Minister of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka. Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my pleasure to extend heartfelt felicitations and warm congratulations on Your Excellency’s appointment as the new Foreign Minister of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka.

I am certain that with your vast experience in leading several portfolios in Sri Lanka’s Government, including as former Foreign Minister and exceptional career spanning politics and academia, you will no doubt succeed in taking Sri Lanka’s foreign relations to new heights.

On this momentous occasion, let me reaffirm our commitment to further enhance the historic relations between Maldives and Sri Lanka. I would also like to express my appreciation for the efforts you have already expended to promote and strengthen the collaboration between our countries in multiple areas.

I look forward to working closely with Your Excellency and the Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka to further strengthen our cooperation in both bilateral and multilateral spheres.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration”.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid holds a virtual meeting with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Thailand
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid holds a virtual meeting with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Thailand
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid holds a virtual meeting with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Thailand

Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Mr. Abdulla Shahid had a virtual call with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Thailand, His Excellency Mr. Don Pramudwinai, today.

During the virtual call, Minister Shahid and Minister Pramudwinai discussed various aspects of the bilateral relations between the two countries.

Both Ministers exchanged views on the COVID-19 pandemic and the measures in place to mitigate its effects and striving towards a complete and comprehensive recovery, in their respective countries. Minister Shahid also thanked the Kingdom of Thailand for the assistance and support provided to the Maldives over the years and during the battle against Covid-19.

The Foreign Ministers expressed confidence in continued cooperation in a wide range of areas of mutual interest especially in education, youth, culture and tourism and reaffirmed their commitment to collaborate more closely at the multilateral sphere, especially within the United Nation.

17th August 2021

On Behalf of the Maldivian people and on my own behalf, I extend sincere congratulations on the jubilant occasion of the 76th Independence Day of the Republic of Indonesia.

I am confident that the strong and mutually beneficial ties that exist between Maldives and Indonesia will grow and strengthen in the years to come. I look forward to working closely with Your Excellency in enhancing friendship between our two peoples and promoting cooperation in various fields.

I wish Your Excellency, good health and continued success in your endeavor to bring growth and prosperity to Indonesia. Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to India

Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to India

Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to India

Minister of Foreign Affairs His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitations ‎‎to Minister of External Affairs His Excellency Dr S Jaishankar, on the occasion of the 75th Independence Day of India.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“Excellency,

On behalf of the Government and people of Maldives, I take great pride in conveying to Your Excellency, Government and the friendly people of the Republic of India, warmest congratulations and best wishes on the jubilant occasion of your 75th Independence Day.

I highly value our expanding partnership, which has deepened and widened over the last three years. Despite the current global challenges, India continues to inspire the world with its unity in diversity in various spheres, including development, governance, technology reform, progress and policy. India has proven to be our “first and best” friend and partner in any crisis, and at any time.

I am confident that, based on the centuries-old traditions of friendship, good neighborliness, mutual respect and trust, we will continue to strengthen the strategic partnership, for the betterment of our countries and peoples, in the interests of ensuring peace, stability and constructive cooperation in the region.

On this day of immense joy and celebration across India, it gives me great pleasure to convey my personal good wishes for your well-being, and for the continued peace, progress and prosperity of the friendly people of India.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: New Non-Resident Ambassador of Republic of Korea to Maldives calls on Foreign Secretary
en.description: New Non-Resident Ambassador of Republic of Korea to Maldives calls on Foreign Secretar
en.body:
New Non-Resident Ambassador of Republic of Korea to Maldives calls on Foreign Secretar

The newly appointed Non-Resident Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to the Maldives, His Excellency Woonjin Jeong called on Foreign Secretary, His Excellency Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today, following the presentation of his credentials to H.E. President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih at a ceremony held this morning at the President’s Office.

At the meeting held in the Ministry this morning, Foreign Secretary Ghafoor congratulated Ambassador Jeong on his appointment and expressed hope that the five decades of long-standing bilateral relations between both the countries would be further strengthened during Ambassador Jeong’s tenure.

Both the Foreign Secretary and Ambassador discussed ways to further strengthen the existing friendly bilateral ties and enhancing collaboration in areas that are of mutual benefit to both countries. Foreign Secretary expressed the appreciation of the Government of Maldives for the scholarships that have been provided by the Government of the Republic of Korea under the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) and expressed interest to explore possibilities for additional scholarship opportunities for Maldivian students.

Foreign Secretary thanked the Government of the Republic of Korea for the generous assistance provided to the Maldives for the fight against the Covid-19 pandemic.

Foreign Secretary Ghafoor was accompanied by Additional Secretary, Mr. Javed Faizal and Executive Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ms.Fathimath Naeema.

en.title: The Government of the United States of America donates Pfizer vaccines to the Maldives
en.description: The Government of the United States of America donates Pfizer vaccines to the Maldives
en.body:
The Government of the United States of America donates Pfizer vaccines to the Maldives

The Government of the United States of America donated 128,700 doses of Pfizer vaccine to the Maldives through the COVAX facility. On behalf of the Government of Maldives, His Excellency Ahmed Naseem, Minister of Health, received the vaccines at a ceremony held today at Velana International Airport.

Speaking at the ceremony, Minister Naseem commended the leadership of the Government of the United States of America on global vaccination efforts and for including the Maldives among the first countries to receive COVID-19 vaccines from the United States. Minister Naseem also thanked the Government of the United States of America for the continuous and unwavering support extended to the Maldives since the beginning of the pandemic and noted that such generosity and friendship have increased the capacity of the Maldives to combat the spread of the virus more effectively.

Minister Naseem also noted that with the donation of Pfizer vaccines, the Government can now start vaccinating children between the ages of 12 and 18 for the very first time. In her remarks, Ambassador Teplitz reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of the United States of America to continue working together to further strengthen the dynamic partnership between the two countries.

The Government of the United States of America has so far contributed over USD 5.4 million to the Maldives COVID-19 response and recovery efforts, including a grant aid of USD 2 million, multiple donations of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), PCR machines, ventilators, and related equipment, as well as donations through several multilateral agencies such as IAEA and UNICEF.

Today's ceremony was attended by Ms. Catherine Haswell, UN Resident Coordinator, Ms. Marjan Montazemi, UNICEF Country Representative, Dr. Nazneen Anwar, WHO Representative along with senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Defence and the Embassy of the United States of America in Colombo.

dv.title: އެމެރިކާ ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ފައިޒާ ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފި
dv.description: އެމެރިކާ ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ފައިޒާ ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފި
dv.body:
އެމެރިކާ ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ފައިޒާ ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފި

ކޮވެކްސް ފެސިލިޓީ މެދުވެރިކޮށް، ޔުނައިޓެޑް ސްޓޭޓްސް އޮފް އެމެރިކާގެ ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް 128،700 (އެއްލައްކަ އަށާވީސް ހާސް ހަތް ސަތޭކަ) ޑޯޒްގެ ފައިޒާ ކޮވިޑް-19 ވެކްސިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ހަދިޔާކޮށްފިއެވެ.

ވެލާނާ އިންޓަނޭޝަނަލް އެއަރޕޯޓްގައި މިއަދު މެންދުރު އޮތް ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ވެކްސިންއާ ހަވާލުވެވަޑައިގަތީ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ހެލްތު، އަހުމަދު ނަސީމް އެވެ. މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން މިނިސްޓަރ ނަސީމް ވަނީ، މުޅި ދުނިޔޭގެ އާބާދީއަށް ވެކްސިން ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އިސްނަގައިގެން ކުރަމުންދާ މަސައްކަތަށް ތަޢުރީފުކުރައްވައި، އެމެރިކާއިން ވެކްސިން އެންމެ ފުރަތަމަ ފޮނުވާ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ހިމެނުއްވީތީ އެމެރިކާ ސަރުކާރަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި ކޮވިޑް-19ގެ ޕެންޑެމިކް ފެށުނީއްސުރެ އެމެރިކާއިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ފޯރުކޮށްދެއްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ ދީލަތި އެހީތަކަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވައި، އެކަށީގެންވާ ގޮތެއްގައި ކޮވިޑް-19 އާ ދެކޮޅަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރުމަށް މި އެހީ ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރަށް މުހިއްމުވިކަން ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

އަދި ފައިޒާ ވެކްސިން ލިބުމުން، އުމުރުން 12 އަހަރާއި 18 އަހަރާ ދެމެދުގެ ކުޑަކުދިންނަށް ވެކްސިން ދޭން ފެށޭނެކަން މިނިސްޓަރ ނަސީމް ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން، އެމެރިކާއިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު، އެލައިނާ ޓެޕްލިޓްޒް ވަނީ ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާ އެމެރިކާ ސަރުކާރާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާކޮށް، ދެޤައުމު ގުޅިގެން އިތުރު މަސައްކަތްތައް ކުރައްވާނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ދެއްވާފައެވެ.

ކޮވިޑް-19 އާ ގުޅިގެން އެމެރިކާ ސަރުކާރުން މިހާތަނަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް 5.4 މިލިއަން އެމެރިކާ ޑޮލަރުގެ އެހީތެރިކަން ފޯރުކޮށްދެއްވާފައިވެއެވެ. އެގޮތުން 2 މިލިއަން އެމެރިކާ ޑޮލަރުގެ ހިލޭ އެހީއާއި، އެކި ފަހަރު މަތިން ގިނަ އަދަދެއްގެ ޕީ.ޕީ.އީ (ޕަރސަނަލް ޕްރޮޓެކްޓިވް އިކުއިޕްމަންޓް) އާއި ޕީ.ސީ.އާރް މެޝިނާއި، ވެންޓިލޭޓަރުގެ އިތުރުން ބޭނުންވާ އެހެނިހެން މެޑިކަލް ސާމާނު ފޯރުކޮށްދީފައިވެއެވެ. އަދި އައި.އޭ.އީ.އޭ އާއި ޔުނިސެފް ފަދަ މަލްޓިލޭޓަރަލް އެޖެންސީތައް މެދުވެރިކޮށްވެސް އެހީ ފޯރުކޮށްދީފައިވެއެވެ.

އެމެރިކާއިން ހަދިޔާކުރި ވެކްސިން ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާ ހަވާލުކުރުމަށް މިއަދު ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި، އދ އިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ރެޒިޑެންޓް ކޯޑިނޭޓަރ ކެތެރިން ހެސްވެލް، ޔުނިސެފް ކަންޓްރީ ރެޕްރެޒެންޓޭޓިވް މަރްޖާން މޮންތަޒޭމީ، ޑަބްލިޔު.އެޗް.އޯ ރެޕްރެޒެންޓޭޓިވް ޑރ ނަޒްނީން އަންވަރު، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއަރޒްއާއި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ހެލްތާއި، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ޑިފެންސްގެ އިސް ބޭފުޅުންނާއި، ކޮޅުނބުގައި ހުންނަ އެމެރިކާ އެމްބަސީގެ އިސް އޮފިޝަލުން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތެވެ.

en.title: Newly appointed Ambassador of Germany to Maldives calls on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
en.description: Newly appointed Ambassador of Germany to Maldives calls on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
en.body:
Newly appointed Ambassador of Germany to Maldives calls on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs

Ambassador of Germany to the Maldives, Holger Seubert called on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, today.

Speaking at the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, State Minister Khaleel congratulated Ambassador Seubert on his appointment and assured the Ambassador that the Maldives will continue to cooperate with Germany in matters of mutual concern such as climate action, strengthening democracy and human rights, and sustainable development.

State Minister Khaleel and Ambassador Seubert further discussed avenues for strengthening bilateral and multilateral relations between the two countries in a wide range of areas.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Shiuneen Rasheed, Joint Secretary, and Mohamed Shujau, Desk Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

en.body:
Newly appointed High Commissioner of Rwanda to Maldives calls on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs

High Commissioner of Rwanda to the Maldives, Jacqueline Mukangira called on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, today.

State Minister Khaleel congratulated High Commissioner Mukangira on her appointment as the first High Commissioner of the Republic of Rwanda to the Republic of Maldives. State Minister Khaleel and High Commissioner Mukangira reiterated commitment on behalf of their respective Governments to work closely together to strengthen bilateral ties and intensify collaboration and exchange between the two countries. State Minister Khaleel highlighted the importance of continuing discussions on the potential for cooperation in areas of mutual importance such as transport, fisheries, agriculture and tourism.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Additional Secretary, Mohamed Faisal and Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Moomina Ibrahim.

High Commissioner Mukangira also held meetings with Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.title: Temporary UK Visa Application Centre opens at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
en.description: Temporary UK Visa Application Centre opens at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
Temporary UK Visa Application Centre opens at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

The temporary United Kingdom Visa Application Centre has started accepting visa applications today at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Visa Centre will collect the biometric enrollments and documents from all applicants who have made prior appointments.

The Visa Application Centre will be open from 2 August 2021 to 4 August 2021.

The Government of the United Kingdom has established the Visa Application Centre in the Maldives on the request of the Government of Maldives, in order to ease the process for those applying for visas, especially students going to the United Kingdom for higher studies. This is part of the government's broader efforts to ease and strengthen the consular services provided to Maldivians.

en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Foreign Minister of Switzerland

en.title: Statement on the Occasion of the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons (TIP) 2021
en.description: Statement on the Occasion of the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons (TIP) 2021
en.body:
Statement on the Occasion of the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons (TIP) 2021

This year, on the occasion of the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons, the Government of Maldives reaffirms its commitment to eliminate human trafficking in all its manifestations. The exploitation of people through trafficking is a grave violation of human rights. It is a global problem that is becoming more complex with increased globalization and rapid advancements in technology and transportation. People of all ages and from all regions are at risk of becoming victims of this heinous crime. The implications of the current COVID-19 pandemic have further increased the vulnerabilities of people to trafficking or the modern form of slavery. It is therefore vital to expand our knowledge on trafficking and ensure the implementation of existing policies to effectively address the intricate issue of trafficking in persons.

Despite the challenges posed by the pandemic, the Government of Maldives has remained persistent in its efforts to combat human trafficking. This has led to the establishment of an Anti-Trafficking in Persons (Anti-TIP) Office at the Ministry of Defence and for the very first time, funds were allocated from the State Budget for the TIP Office and the National Action Plan (NAP) to improve anti-trafficking activities. President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih ratified the second amendment to Article 12 and Article 14 of the Maldives Anti-Human Trafficking Act (Act no. 12/2013) to align the definition of human trafficking with that of the 2000 UN TIP Protocol. A victim shelter has also been set up in Gulhifalhu to provide a secure refuge to victims of human trafficking. Furthermore, the Maldives held its first-ever social media awareness campaign on International Migrant’s Day to raise awareness of the severity of human trafficking.

As a result of such initiatives, the Maldives has been upgraded this year to Tier 2 in the US State Department’s Trafficking in Persons Report 2021, after remaining on the Tier 2 Watch List for three consecutive years. This upgrade is a clear testament to the progress attained by the Government in the past year in its fight against human trafficking. Acknowledging the positive developments achieved in promoting and protecting human rights, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office of the United Kingdom has also removed the Maldives from its list of Human Rights Priority Countries.

On this World Day Against Trafficking in Persons, the Government reiterates its commitment to strengthening its efforts to comprehensively address trafficking in persons, which has been a deep-rooted issue with a long history of systematic failures in border management. The Government also remains committed to supporting the first responders against human trafficking, by providing them with resources and support, and ensuring justice for the victims of this serious crime that threatens human rights and human dignity.

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid meets his Bulgarian counterpart Svetlan Hristov Stoev
en.description: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid meets his Bulgarian counterpart Svetlan Hristov Stoev
en.body:
Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid meets his Bulgarian counterpart Svetlan Hristov Stoev

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid has met with Foreign Minister of Bulgaria, Svetlan Hristov Stoev, this afternoon.

At the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bulgaria today, both the Ministers discussed on strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two countries in a wide range of areas.

The Ministers also reiterated commitment to further strengthen the bilateral partnership between the two countries in areas of mutual interest for both countries in the bilateral and multilateral fora.

Foreign Minister Shahid also acknowledged the role played by Bulgaria in the European Union and highlighted the pivotal role played by the European Union in reviving democracy in the Maldives and assured the Government’s commitment to support this partnership in the future.

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid meets Tourism Minister of Bulgaria
en.description: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid meets Tourism Minister of Bulgaria
en.body:
Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid meets Tourism Minister of Bulgaria

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid has met the Tourism Minister of Bulgaria, Dr. Stella Baltova, today.

At the meeting held at the Ministry of Tourism today, both the Ministers discussed ways to further strengthen and enhance the existing bilateral relations and exploring opportunities to widen cooperation in the tourism sector between the two countries. Foreign Minister Shahid noted the increase in tourists arriving from Bulgaria to the Maldives and expressed hope to see further promotion of Maldivian tourism in Bulgaria and to see even more tourists from Bulgaria arriving in the Maldives.

Both Ministers discussed the measures taken to curb the spread of COVID-19 in the two countries and noted the importance of strong and comprehensive policies in addressing the pandemic.

Foreign Minister Shahid also briefed the Minister on his priorities for his Presidency of Hope as the President of the 76th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, noting that it was important for countries to come together to find a way out of the pandemic.

Minister Baltova noted the importance of increasing connectivity for the promotion of tourism and expressed hope to see more transport connections between Bulgaria and the Maldives and discussed further avenues for promotion of tourism cooperation between the two countries.

Foreign Minister Shahid was accompanied by High Commissioner of Maldives to the United Kingdom, Dr. Farahanaz Faizal and Third Secretary at the High Commission of Maldives in the United Kingdom, Mariyam Afnaan.

en.body:
Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid holds meeting with Minister of Transport, Information Technology and Communications of Bulgaria

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid held a meeting with the Minister of Transport, Information Technology and Communications of Bulgaria, Georgi Todorov, this afternoon.

At the discussions held at the Ministry of Transport, Information Technology and Communications of Bulgaria, both Ministers discussed the importance of improving information and communication networks and transport networks in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. Foreign Minister Shahid highlighted the importance of strong and reliable information and communication networks for the implementation of the Government’s decentralisation policies.

The Ministers also noted the increasing number of tourist arrivals from Bulgaria to the Maldives and discussed avenues for further increasing transport links for stronger people to people connection between the two countries.

Minister Todorov was accompanied by senior officials of the Ministry of Transport, Information Technology and Communication of Bulgaria.

Foreign Minister Shahid also held a meeting with the Deputy Minister of Economy of Bulgaria, Kalina Konstantinova, this afternoon.

At the meeting held at the Ministry of Economy, discussions were held on further enhancing economic and trade ties between the two countries, including exporting Maldivian fish products to Bulgaria.

Deputy Minister Konstantinova was accompanied by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bulgaria Zaritsa Dinkova and senior officials of the Ministry of Economy of Bulgaria.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by High Commissioner of Maldives to the United Kingdom, Dr. Farahanaz Faizal and Third Secretary at the High Commission of Maldives to the United Kingdom, Mariyam Afnaan.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Peru

Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Peru

Minister’s message reads as follows:

It is my sincere hope that the friendly relations that exist between our two countries will be maintained and further strengthened in the future.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress of the people of the Republic of Peru and the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid departs to Bulgaria on an official visit
en.description: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid departs to Bulgaria on an official visit
en.body:
Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid departs to Bulgaria on an official visit

Minister of Foreign Affairs and President-elect of the 76th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, Abdulla Shahid departs to Bulgaria on an official visit from 27 to 29 July 2021.

During the visit, Minister Shahid will meet with Foreign Minister Svetlan Hristov Stoev and hold bilateral talks to explore avenues for cooperation to fortify the existing bilateral relations between both countries.

Minister Shahid will also meet with Minister of Tourism of Bulgaria and other senior officials from the Government of Bulgaria and explore opportunities to enhance cooperation in various sectors between the two countries.

During this visit, Minister Shahid will also share his vision for his Presidency of Hope and discuss his priorities for the 76th Session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Minister Shahid is accompanied by High Commissioner of Maldives to the United Kingdom, Dr. Farahanaz Faizal and Third Secretary at the High Commission of Maldives to the United Kingdom, Mariyam Afnaan.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Liberia

en.title: Minister Shahid outlines his vision for the Presidency of Hope at the Indian Council for World Affairs
en.description: Minister Shahid outlines his vision for the Presidency of Hope at the Indian Council for World Affairs
en.body:
Minister Shahid outlines his vision for the Presidency of Hope at the Indian Council for World Affairs

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, and President-elect of the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly Abdulla Shahid, outlined his vision and his priorities for the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly, while delivering the 38th Sapru House Lecture at the Indian Council of World Affairs, on the topic “Presidency of Hope: 76th UNGA - COVID pandemic and need for reformed multilateralism”, today.

Minister Shahid spoke in detail about his five “rays of hope”: Recovering from COVID19, Rebuilding Sustainably, Responding to the Needs of the Planet, Respecting the Rights of All, and Reforming the United Nations. These areas, he noted, spoke to the most pressing challenges of the time.

He also spoke on the need for a forward looking agenda – a “Presidency of Hope”. He noted that this was a world in despair, suffering from devastation, with the COVID19 pandemic still raging on. He also noted that against this bleakness, it is hope that will drive people forward, and what will make people stand up and get moving again.

Minister Shahid also highlighted the importance of multilateralism in general, and the United Nations in particular, in building a more resilient, stronger world. He noted that the United Nations’ strength lies in its ability to shape norms, change discourse, and forge consensus. He also highlighted the convening power of the United Nations. In this, Minister Shahid noted, lies the opportunity for the United Nations to increase its effectiveness and efficiency, in delivering for people, for the planet and for prosperity.

The 38th Sapru House Lecture was moderated by Former Deputy Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations Ambassador Manjeev Puri. Minister Shahid was introduced by Director General of the Indian Council for World Affairs Dr T C A Raghavan.

en.title: Minister Shahid calls on Prime Minister of India
en.description: This is Minister Shahid's first visit in his official capacity as President-elect of the UN General Assembly.
en.body:
This is Minister Shahid's first visit in his official capacity as President-elect of the UN General Assembly.

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives and President-elect of the 76th United Nations General Assembly, Abdulla Shahid called on Prime Minister of the Republic of India Narendra Modi today.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid conveyed greetings and good wishes to Prime Minister Modi, the Government, and people of India, on behalf of President Solih and the Government, and people of the Maldives. Minister Shahid expressed appreciation to the Indian Government for the continuous support and assistance offered to the Maldives, especially during COVID19 pandemic.

Further, the Minister also thanked the Indian Government for the support rendered to the Maldives candidacy for the Presidency of the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly. Minister Shahid briefed Prime Minister Modi on his priorities during 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly, and the main themes of the Presidency of Hope.

Minister Shahid was accompanied at the call by High Commissioner of Maldives to India Dr Hussain Niyaaz and Chef-de-Cabinet-designate of the Office of the President of the 76th United Nations General Assembly Ambassador Nagaraj Naidu.

The Minister is on an official visit to Delhi from 22-24 July 2021, on invitation of the Indian Government. This is his first visit in his official capacity as President-elect of the General Assembly.

en.title: Maldives and India sign a renewed Memorandum of Understanding on High Impact Community Development Projects
en.description: The renewed MoU increases the size of the Indian grant assistance to High Impact Community Development Projects in the Maldives, to 155 million Rufiya
en.body:
The renewed MoU increases the size of the Indian grant assistance to High Impact Community Development Projects in the Maldives, to 155 million Rufiya

The Governments of Maldives and India have today, signed a renewed Memorandum of Understanding on Indian Grant Assistance for Implementation of High Impact Community Development Projects through local bodies. The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives Abdulla Shahid, and the Minister of External Affairs of India Dr S Jaishankar signed the MoU on behalf of their respective Governments.

The renewed MoU increases the size of the Indian grant assistance to High Impact Community Development Projects in the Maldives, to 155 million Rufiya (equivalent to approximately US$10 million). Previously, the grant assistance was up to MVR 85 million.

The MoU was first signed on 17 March 2019, during the official visit of then Minister of External Affairs of India late Sushma Swaraj to the Maldives. The aim of this MoU is to set up the framework to support small and effective developmental initiatives which will be implemented through local bodies, government-to-government institutions; and jointly work towards successful implementation of small projects which contribute to economic and social development and improvement of public welfare.

The primary themes of projects covered under the MoU are socio-economic development, livelihood activity, conservation of environmental and cultural heritage, empowerment of women and child welfare and skills development.

Twelve projects are currently underway, under the High Impact Community Development Project grant scheme. They include the establishment of Geydhoshu Mas Plant (Neighbourhood Fish Processing Plants) in Hithadhoo, Maradhoo and Hulhudhoo of Addu City, and Noonu Kendhikulhudhoo; Development of tourism zones in Hithadhoo, Feydhoo, Maradhoo, Meedhoo and Hulhudhoo of Addu City; Agricultural Linkages Project in Hanimaadhoo by the Ministry of Fisheries, Agriculture and Marine Resources; Establishing a drug detox centre in Addu City Hulhudhoo; Establishing a Water Bottling Factory in Haa Alif Hoarafushi.

The Maldives and Belgium have cooperated in areas of mutual interest, such as climate action, strengthening democracy, and human rights. I thank Your Excellency, the People and the Government of Belgium for the assistance provided to the Maldives at all times, in various fora.

I remain confident that the Maldives-Belgium relations will continue to strengthen in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health, wellbeing and, progress and prosperity for the people of Belgium.”

en.title: Embassy of Maldives in Brussels hosts ‘Investment in the Maldives’ Webinar
en.description: Embassy of Maldives in Brussels hosts ‘Investment in the Maldives’ Webinar
en.body:
Embassy of Maldives in Brussels hosts ‘Investment in the Maldives’ Webinar

Embassy of the Maldives in Brussels in collaboration with Hub Brussels, organized a webinar entitled “Investment in the Maldives”, facilitated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology, Ministry of Fisheries, Marine Resources and Agriculture as well as the Ministry of Economic Development and Maldives Fund Management Corporation today.

The Government agencies provided an overview of Maldives post-Covid economic recovery priorities and investment opportunities from their respective sectors. With participation close to 90 economic sector specialists and potential investors based in EU Countries, the webinar provided an important platform to accelerate commercial diplomacy of the Maldives with the Kingdom of Belgium, Kingdom of the Netherlands and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. The webinar also supports the government’s continued initiatives to strengthen trade and investment, provide information to foreign investors, and facilitate networking between relevant government agencies and foreign investors.

As the Keynote Speaker of the event, the Vice President of European Investment Bank, Mr. Christian Kettel Thomsen reiterated the continued assistance from the EIB to the Maldives in his keynote address. Also speaking at the event was the Minister of Tourism of the Maldives, H.E. Dr. Abdulla Mausoom, who highlighted the Government's priority to build better, stronger, and greener in moving forward. Speaking at the event, Minister of Finance H.E. Mr. Ibrahim Ameer also thanked the European Investment Bank and the Kingdom of Belgium for their assistance extended to the government of Maldives during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Speaking at the webinar, Foreign Secretary H.E. Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed emphasized that Embassy in Brussels remains eager to help investors to explore how to contribute to our long-standing economic and commercial relationship and thanked H.E. Ambassador Hassan Sobir, and his dynamic team for organizing this timely and important webinar.

en.title: The High Commissioner of Bangladesh to Maldives Calls on Foreign Minister
en.description: The High Commissioner of Bangladesh to Maldives Calls on Foreign Minister
en.body:
The High Commissioner of Bangladesh to Maldives Calls on Foreign Minister

High Commissioner of Bangladesh to the Maldives, Rear Admiral Mohammad Nazmul Hassan called on Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs this afternoon, Foreign Minister and the High Commissioner exchanged views on the current situation of the Covid-19 pandemic and discussed the respective national approaches in dealing with its challenges, including vaccination.

Foreign Minister Shahid expressed appreciation to the Government of Bangladesh for the generous assistance extended to the Maldives in combating Covid-19 on multiple fronts. Minister Shahid noted in particular the services of the medical team of the Bangladesh Armed Forces who stayed in Maldives for over four months, assisting in the Government’s vaccination programme.

Minister Shahid also thanked the Government of Bangladesh for supporting his candidature as the President of the seventy-sixth session of the UN General Assembly.

Foreign Minister Shahid and High Commissioner Nazmul Hassan acknowledged the strengthening of Bangladesh – Maldives bilateral relations, as evidenced by the recent State Visit of His Excellency President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih in March and Minister’s official visit in February this year.

Foreign Minister Shahid and High Commissioner Nazmul Hassan reiterated their commitment to working closely together to enhance cooperation and collaboration in areas that are of mutual benefit to both countries.

en.title: President dedicates Ministry of Foreign Affairs building in memory of former Foreign Minister Fathulla Jameel
en.description: Ministry of Foreign Affairs building dedicated in memory of former Foreign Minister Fathulla Jameel
en.body:
Ministry of Foreign Affairs building dedicated in memory of former Foreign Minister Fathulla Jameel

A Special Ceremony was held this morning, to dedicate the Ministry of Foreign Affairs building in memory of the late Uz. Fathulla Jameel, Order of the Distinguished Rule of Izuddin (O.D.R.I). The honour was solemnised by the President of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih who unveiled the name of the building as “Fathulla Jameel Building” as well as a special plaque placed inside the building, in recognition of Uz. Fathulla Jameel’s long and distinguished service to the nation.

Speaking at the ceremony, President Solih said that today was historic day for the Maldives Foreign Service, following the renovation of the foreign ministry building which had been underway since 2019. The President congratulated the Foreign Service and its members for their hard work, dedication and undeterred commitment to serve, even during the most arduous times in the midst of a pandemic, to ensure that the Maldives engaged globally to secure vital supplies, medical equipment and most importantly, vaccines. He thanked the current Foreign Minister, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, for his leadership of the Service during his tenure and reaffirmed his confidence in Minister Shahid for his invaluable efforts in engaging with the international community and in further enhancing the Maldives’ own diplomatic outreach and its relations with the outside world.

Minister Shahid thanked President Solih for his decision to honour the life of Hon. Fathulla Jameel. He praised former Minister Fathulla Jameel as a visionary whom he had the honour of serving with as a junior Foreign Service Officer. He said that the foundations of the modern Maldivian Foreign Service was established and promoted by Fathulla Jameel, who always believed that a small country like the Maldives, should have a professional, skilled and efficient diplomatic service that could promote international relations, trade, tourism and our interactions with the international community.

The twin daughters of the late Uz. Fathulla Jameel, conveyed a video message on behalf of the family, that expressed the importance their late father attached to the Maldives Foreign Ministry and the Maldivian Foreign Policy during his long and illustrious tenure. Today’s ceremony was also attended by the Vice-President His Excellency Faisal Naseem, Chief Justice Uz. Muthasim Adnan, Deputy Speaker of the People’s Majlis Hon. Eva Abdulla, members of the Cabinet, the Diplomatic Corp, former and present members of the Maldives Foreign Service.

Hon. Fathulla Jameel became the Foreign Minister in 1978 and went on to serve until 2005, becoming the longest serving Foreign Minister in the Maldives, and one of the longest serving in the world at 27 years of service. He was educated in Al-Azhar University in Cairo, and prior to becoming the Foreign Minister, also served as the Permanent Representative of Maldives to the United Nations in New York. He passed away in 2012 at the age of 69.

The Foreign Ministry building was first designed by Hon. Fathulla Jameel in the early 2000s, and construction of the complex was completed in 2005. Renovation of the existing building commenced in 2019 and was handed over to the Government of Maldives in early 2021. The initial construction and renovation of the building was done with the assistance of the Government of the People’s Republic of China.

en.title: Japan provides Grant Aid of 110 Million Japanese Yen to the Maldives to the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship
en.description: Japan provides Grant Aid of 110 Million Japanese Yen to the Maldives to the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship
en.body:
Japan provides Grant Aid of 110 Million Japanese Yen to the Maldives to the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship

The Government of Maldives and the Government of Japan has signed the Exchange of Notes to provide a grant aid of 110 Million Japanese Yen (approximately USD 998,000) to the Maldives for the continuation of scholarships opportunities to be offered by the Government of Japan for the fiscal year 2022 under the Japanese Project for Human Resource Development (JDS). The Minister of Foreign Affairs His Excellency Abdulla Shahid and Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives Her Excellency Keiko Yanai signed the Notes today at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The grant aid will be utilized to provide 6 scholarships to the Maldives again this year, a project which was implemented last year by the Government of Japan for further promoting the Human Resource Development in the Maldives. This is the second year that Japan has provided the Maldives with grant assistance pertaining to human resource development, with the initial agreement signed in 2020.

Officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Embassy of Japan and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) attended the ceremony.

en.title: High Commissioner of Sri Lanka pays farewell call on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: High Commissioner of Sri Lanka pays farewell call on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
High Commissioner of Sri Lanka pays farewell call on Minister of Foreign Affairs

The High Commissioner of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka to the Maldives, His Excellency Rohana Beddage made his farewell call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, this afternoon at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. High Commissioner Beddage has served as the High Commissioner to the Maldives since 31 August 2020.

Foreign Minister Shahid conveyed sincere gratitude and appreciation for his services and efforts to strengthen bilateral ties between the Maldives and Sri Lanka, during his tenure. High Commissioner Rohana Beddage thanked the Government and people of Maldives for the continuous support and hospitality accorded to him during his stay in the Maldives.

Foreign Minister Shahid was accompanied by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, Foreign Secretary, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, and Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Fathimath Ghina.

en.title: British High Commissioner calls on Minister Shahid
en.description: British High Commissioner calls on Minister Shahid
en.body:
British High Commissioner calls on Minister Shahid

British High Commissioner to the Maldives Caron Rohsler paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, today.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid expressed the Government's appreciation for removing the Maldives from the "Human Rights priority list" in the 2020 Human Rights and Democracy report issued by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. Minister Shahid noted that this was a testament to the progress the Maldives has made in these areas.

Minister Shahid further thanked the High Commissioner for the assistance provided to the Maldives in the lead up to the COP26 to be held in Glasgow, Scotland, later this year. Minister Shahid noted the exemplary chairmanship of the Commonwealth by the United Kingdom and reiterated the support of the Maldives for further strengthening the Commonwealth.

Speaking at the meeting, High Commissioner Rohsler reaffirmed the support of the United Kingdom to key areas of interest for the Maldives, such as climate action, counter terrorism, and defence cooperation.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to France
en.description: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to France
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to France

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of greetings to Jean-Yves Le Drian, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of the French Republic, on the festive occasion of the National Day of France.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the People, the Government of the Maldives, and on my own behalf, it is my great pleasure to extend warm wishes to Your Excellency, the People and the Government of the French Republic on the joyous occasion of the National Day of France on the 14th of July.

Since the establishment of diplomatic relations on 20 May 1969, France has been a close friend and partner in the democratic and development journey of the Maldives. This five-decade long relationship has been highlighted with close cooperation in several key areas such as climate change, environmental protection and counter terrorism.

The Maldives also welcomes thousands of French travelers to its shores every year and we look forward to continuing to do so in the years to come. I am confident that this relation will grow from strength to strength in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your continued well-being and the assurances of my highest considerations.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Revolution Day greetings to Iraq
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Revolution Day greetings to Iraq
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Revolution Day greetings to Iraq

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sent a message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Iraq, Fuad Mohammad Hussein, on the occasion of the Revolution Day of Iraq.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

I remain assured that the spirit of close cooperation and collaboration which exists between our two countries will continue to strengthen and expand as we go forward. Please accept my best wishes for the continued advancement, success, and prosperity for the people of Iraq.

en.title: India gifts vehicles to support Maldives Correctional Service
en.description: India gifts vehicles to support Maldives Correctional Service
en.body:
India gifts vehicles to support Maldives Correctional Service

Vehicles procured with the financial support of the Indian Government were gifted to Maldives Correctional Service in a virtual ceremony held today.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, the High Commissioner of India to the Maldives Sunjay Sudhir, and Commissioner of Prisons Ahmed Mohamed Fulhu spoke at the ceremony. Senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Maldives Correctional Service and the High Commission of India in Maldives also participated in the ceremony.

The Maldives Correctional Service was allocated a total of 8 million Rufiya from Indian grant assistance, to procure vehicles to ease the transportation issues and increase the capacity of Maldives Correctional Service to undertake its responsibilities effectively. The first component was the procurement of land vehicles. A total of four vehicles (3 vans and 1 car) were procured under this component. The second component of this project to procure a passenger launch is ongoing.

Speaking at the event, Minister Shahid highlighted the crucial role played by Maldives Correctional Service in the reform and reintegration of offenders back to society as productive citizens, and alluded to the importance of increasing the effectiveness of the institution in providing its services to the people of Maldives.

The financial support has been provided from the grant assistance of USD 6.9 million (MVR 106 million) granted to the Government of Maldives by the Government of India during the visit of the Minister of External Affairs of India in March 2019. The aim of the grant assistance is to conduct socio-economic development projects across the country which make a significant impact. The projects under this grant will be managed by local authorities.

dv.title: އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުން ހަދިޔާކުރި ވެހިކަލްތައް ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސްއާ ހަވާލުކޮށްފި
dv.description: އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުން ހަދިޔާކުރި ވެހިކަލްތައް ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސްއާ ހަވާލުކޮށްފި
dv.body:
އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުން ހަދިޔާކުރި ވެހިކަލްތައް ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސްއާ ހަވާލުކޮށްފި

އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގެ ދަށުން މޯލްޑިވްސް ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސް އަށް ހޯދާފައިވާ ވެހިކަލްތައް، އެ ސަރވިސްއާއި ރަސްމީކޮށް މިއަދު ހަވާލުކޮށްފިއެވެ.

މިކަމަށްޓަކައި މިއަދު ވަރޗުއަލްކޮށް ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއަރޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދު އާއި، އިންޑިއާއިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު ސަންޖޭ ސުދީރުގެ އިތުރުން ކަމިޝަނަރ އޮފް ޕްރިޒަންސް އަހުމަދު މުހައްމަދުފުޅު ވާހަކަފުޅު ދެއްކެވިއެވެ. މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއަރޒްއާއި އިންޑިއާ ހައިކޮމިޝަންގެ އިތުރުން މޯލްޑިވްސް ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސް ގެ އިސް ބޭފުޅުން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތެވެ.

ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސްގެ މަސައްކަތް ފުރިހަމަ ގޮތުގައި ކުރުމަށް އަދި ދަތުރުފަތުރުކުރުމަށް އެސަރވިސްއަސް ދިމާވެފައިވާ ދަތިތަކުން އަރައިގަތުމަށް، އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގެ ދަށުން މޯލްޑިވްސް ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސް އަށް ބޭނުންވާ އުޅަނދުފަހަރު ހޯދުމަށް 8 މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ ވަނީ ހަމަޖައްސާފައެވެ. މި މަސައްކަތުގެ ފުރަތަމަ ބައިގެ ދަށުން 4 އެއްގަމު އުޅަނދު ( 3 ވޭން، 1 ކާރު) މިހާރު ހޯދާފައިވާއިރު، ކަނޑުމަގުން ދަތުރުކުރުމަށް ސްޕީޑް ބޯޓެއް ހޯދުމުގެ މަސައްކަތް މިހާރު ދަނީ ކުރިއަށެވެ.

މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު ވަނީ، ކުށްވެރިން އަލުން އަނބުރާ މުޖްތަމައަށް ބޭނުންތެރި ބައެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ނެރެދިނުމަށް ކަރެކްޝަނަލް ސަރވިސްއިން ކުރަމުންދާ މުހިއްމު މަސައްކަތް ފާހަގަކުރައްވައި، ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް މުހިއްމި ޚިދުމަތެއް ފޯރުކޮށްދެމުންދާ އެ ސަރވިސްއިން ފޯރުކޮށްދޭ ޚިދުމަތްތައް އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމަށް އެމުއައްސަސާގެ ޤާބިލްކަން އިތުރުކުރުމުގެ މުހިއްމުކަމުގެ މައްޗަށް އަލިއަޅުއްވާލައްވާފައެވެ.

މި ޕްރޮޖެކްޓަކީ 2019 ވަނަ އަހަރު އިންޑިއާގެ އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއަރޒް މިނިސްޓަރ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކުރެއްވި ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިއުލާންކުރެއްވި 106 މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގެ ތެރެއިން ކުރިއަށްގެންދެވުނު ޕްރޮޖެކްޓެކެވެ.

dv.title: ނިއުޒިލެންޑުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު، ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދުއާއި ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފި
dv.description: ނިއުޒިލެންޑުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު، ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދުއާއި ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފި
dv.body:
ނިއުޒިލެންޑުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު، ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދުއާއި ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފި

ނިއުޒިލޭންޑުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު ޖޯ ޓިންޑޯލް، ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދު އާ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ. ވަރޗުއަލްކޮށް މިއަދު ހެނދުނު ބޭއްވި މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި، ކޮވިޑް-19ގެ ސަބަބުން ދިމާވެފައިވާ މާލީ އަދި އިޤްތިޞާދީ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުންނާއި، ދެޤައުމުގައި ވެކްސިން ޕްރޮގްރާމް ކުރިއަށްގެންދާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ދެބޭފުޅުން މަޝްވަރާކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

އަދި ދެޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އޮތް ގާތް ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކޮށް، ދެޤައުމުންވެސް އިސްކަންދޭ ކަންކަމުގައި އެކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރުމާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ދެ ބޭފުޅުން މަޝްވަރާކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އެގޮތުން ފަތުރުވެރިކަމާއި، ކައުންޓަރ ޓެރަރިޒަމް އަދި ތިމާވެއްޓާއި މޫސުމީ ބަދަލުތަކާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ދެބޭފުޅުން މަޝްވަރާކުރެއްވިއެވެ. ހަމައެއާއެކު، މަލްޓިލޭޓަރަލް ފޯރަމްތަކުގައި ދެޤައުމު ގުޅިގެން އިތުރަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރުމާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރާއި ސަފީރު މަޝްވަރާކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Comoros
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Comoros
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Comoros

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Comoros, Dhoihir Dhoulkamal on the occasion of the Independence Day of the Union of the Comoros.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“Allow me to extend warm greetings and felicitations to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Comoros on the triumphant occasion of your Independence Day.

I am confident that the blossoming relations between Maldives and Comoros will continue to prosper and flourish.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends message of felicitations to Ðorđe Radulović, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro, on the occasion of the Statehood Day of Montenegro.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Montenegro, on the joyous occasion of the statehood day of Montenegro.

It is my sincere hope that the friendly relations that exist between our two countries will be maintained and further strengthened in the future.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration”

en.body:

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Kiribati
en.description: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Kiribati
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Kiribati

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives Abdulla Shahid sends message of felicitations to Taneti Maamau, President, Head of Government and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Immigration of the Republic of Kiribati, on the occasion of their National Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to convey warm greetings and sincere good wishes of the Government and the People of Maldives, and those of my own, to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Kiribati, on the occasion of your 42nd National Day.

As fellow SIDS, I look forward to strengthening the friendly relations between our two countries and enhancing collaboration at the multilateral front.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress of the people of Kiribati and the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Vice Admiral Chawla, Flag Officer, Commanding in Chief, Southern Naval Command, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: Vice Admiral Chawla, Flag Officer, Commanding in Chief, Southern Naval Command, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
Vice Admiral Chawla, Flag Officer, Commanding in Chief, Southern Naval Command, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs

Vice Admiral Anil Kumar Chawla, Flag Officer, Commanding in Chief, Southern Naval Command of the Indian Navy, called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid today. The meeting was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The Minister welcomed Vice Admiral Chawla to the Maldives and reflected on the historically strong bilateral relations between the Maldives and India, particularly in the field of Defence and Security cooperation. He also noted important role played by the Indian Armed Forces in enhancing and developing the capacity of the Maldives National Defence Force. The Minister and Vice Admiral Chawla discussed the importance of cooperation between countries in maintain peace and security in the Indian Ocean Region. The Minister further reaffirmed commitment of the Government of the Maldives to focusing on strengthening maritime safety and security in the Indian Ocean Region.

The Minister was accompanied by the Foreign Secretary, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed and Joint Secretary, India Division, Mariyam Midhfa Naeem at the meeting.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to South Sudan
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to South Sudan
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to South Sudan

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of South Sudan, Beatrice Khamisa Wani-Noah on the occasion of the Independence Day of South Sudan.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my pleasure to extend warm felicitations and well wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of South Sudan on the jubilant occasion of your Independence Day.

en.title: Maldives Receives Aid from Pakistan through the SAARC COVID-19 Emergency Fund
en.description: A cheque symbolising the grant was handed over to Foreign Minister Shahid by High Commissioner of Pakistan, Vice Admiral Ather Mukhtar at a meeting held today
en.body:
A cheque symbolising the grant was handed over to Foreign Minister Shahid by High Commissioner of Pakistan, Vice Admiral Ather Mukhtar at a meeting held today

The Government of Pakistan has donated MVR 5,958,781.44 (USD 386,432) to the Government of Maldives, to assist in its Covid-19 response and recovery efforts.

A cheque symbolising the grant was handed over to Foreign Minister Shahid by High Commissioner of Pakistan, Vice Admiral Ather Mukhtar at a meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today.

The contribution was made by Pakistan through the SAARC COVID-19 Emergency Fund, established in March 2020 during a virtual summit of the SAARC Heads of States and Governments, held in response to the global coronavirus pandemic. The Emergency Fund is financed by voluntary contributions from all SAARC countries. The initiative seeks to address the challenges and mitigate the risks associated with the coronavirus pandemic in the South Asian region.

On behalf of President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, the Government and people of Maldives Minister Shahid extended sincere gratitude to Prime Minister Imran Khan, the Government and the people of Pakistan for the generous financial support. Minister Shahid noted this gesture demonstrates the special regard and consideration Pakistan accords to Maldives.

en.title: The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the International Maritime Organization presents her Letter of Credence
en.description: The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the International Maritime Organization presents Letter of Credence to the Secretary-General of the IMO
en.body:
The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the International Maritime Organization presents Letter of Credence to the Secretary-General of the IMO

The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the International Maritime Organization (IMO), Dr. Farahanaz Faizal, presented her Letter of Credence to the Secretary-General of the International Maritime Organization, Mr. Kitack Lim, in an official ceremony held at the Headquarters of IMO today. High Commissioner Dr. Farahanz Faizal is the first Permanent Representative of the Maldives to be accredited to the IMO since the Maldives became a Member State of the organization in 1967.

At the ceremony, High Commissioner Dr. Farahanaz Faizal thanked Secretary-General Kitack Lim for the warm welcome, and conveyed compliments from President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. She reiterated the Government of Maldives’ commitment towards closer engagement with the IMO in a number of areas, including the safe, fair and effective regulating of shipping as well as the reduction of pollution from ships, in line with internationally agreed regulations and standards.

The President of the Republic of Maldives, Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, appointed High Commissioner Dr. Farahanaz Faizal, as the Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the International Maritime Organization on 5 April 2021, following approval by the People’s Majlis of the Republic of Maldives on 2 March 2021.

Established on 17 March 1948, the International Maritime Organization is a United Nations specialized agency, responsible for the safety and security of shipping and the prevention of marine and atmospheric pollution by ships. It aims to create a regulatory framework for the shipping industry that is fair and effective, universally adopted and universally implemented. At present, IMO has 174 Member States and 3 Associate Members. The Maldives joined IMO on 31 May 1967.

en.title: Foreign Secretary Ghafoor reiterates the Maldives’ commitment to reaching full equality for women in actions to address climate change, at the high-level event on the Action Coalition on Feminist Action for Climate Justice
en.description: Foreign Secretary Ghafoor reiterates the Maldives’ commitment to reaching full equality for women in actions to address climate change
en.body:
Foreign Secretary Ghafoor reiterates the Maldives’ commitment to reaching full equality for women in actions to address climate change

The Foreign Secretary of the Republic of Maldives, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, participated in the virtual high-level event on the Action Coalition on Feminist Action for Climate Justice today. The high-level event took place during the Generation Equality Forum, which was held virtually in Paris from 30 June to 2 July 2021.

In his statement, Foreign Secretary Ghafoor outlined the Maldives’ commitments under the four actions laid out in the blueprint of the Feminist Action for Climate Justice. He stated that the Maldives commits to; expanding the fiscal authorities given to local councils and women’s development councils towards climate-related funding, increasing women in leadership and policy-formulation positions, by building capacity through tools and resources, developing the capacity at community-level and/or grassroots actors to engage in climate related planning processes, and improving data collection, towards exploring climate impacts in terms of loss and damage, specifically the impacts on women and women-led enterprises. He further acknowledged the disproportionate effect climate change has on women and reiterated Maldives’ commitment to reaching full equality for women in actions to address climate change.

The Generation Equality Forum was convened by UN Women and co-hosted by the Governments of France and Mexico in partnership with civil society and youth organizations. Out of the six Action Coalitions established under the Forum, the Maldives and Costa Rica co-leads the Action Coalition on Feminist Action for Climate Justice.

en.title: The Maldives Warranted an Improved Ranking in the U.S. Department of State’s 2021 Trafficking in Persons Report
en.description: The Maldives Warranted an Improved Ranking in the U.S. Department of State’s 2021 Trafficking in Persons Report
en.body:
The Maldives Warranted an Improved Ranking in the U.S. Department of State’s 2021 Trafficking in Persons Report

The Maldives has been upgraded to Tier 2 in the U.S. Department of State's 21st annual Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, released by the U.S. Secretary of State on Thursday tonight.

This upgrade comes after the Maldives remained on the Tier 2 Watch List for three consecutive years. It is a clear demonstration of the progress attained by the Government of Maldives in its fight against human trafficking.

The 2021 TIP Report, in particular, highlighted the accelerated efforts of the Government of Maldives to increase its anti-trafficking capacity despite the adverse implications posed by the COVID-19 pandemic. These efforts include the strengthened implementation of the National Anti-Human Trafficking Action Plan, along with the timely establishment of the Office of Anti-Human Trafficking (ATO). The Report also commended the amendment made to Article 16(b) of the Prevention of Human Trafficking Act (PHTA), adding revisions to align the human trafficking definition with that of the 2000 UN TIP Protocol. The Government was further credited for elevating the role of law enforcement authorities to better address human trafficking cases and for the measures undertaken to support and protect the trafficking of victims. The Government of Maldives is committed to making tangible improvements to its anti-trafficking efforts especially within the key areas identified in the TIP Report. The Government also seeks to enhance cooperation with its international partners to resolve the challenges faced in eliminating the complex crime of human trafficking, at all fronts.

The TIP Report is an annual assessment issued by the U.S. Department of State to monitor and combat human trafficking worldwide. It ranks states into tiers based on the state's compliance with standards outlined in the U.S. Trafficking Victims Protection Act (TVPA) 2000. The goal of this report is to stimulate action and create partnerships around the world in the fight against trafficking in persons.

en.title: High Commission of Maldives in Singapore and National Association of Travel Agents Singapore co-hosts “Destination Maldives Webinar”

en.body:
High Commission of Maldives in Singapore and National Association of Travel Agents Singapore co-hosts “Destination Maldives Webinar

The High Commission of Maldives in Singapore, in coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and National Association of Travel Agents Singapore (NATAS) organized a webinar today reiterating Maldives’s preparedness and readiness to welcome Singaporean tourists, as Singapore prepares to re-open its borders for the Maldives.

The webinar also provided an important platform to brief the Singapore’s tourism industry on the new guidelines and safety protocols in place for international tourists arriving into the Maldives. Discussion also ensued on how to collaborate with tourism stakeholders in Maldives and build a closer relationship with Singapore’s travel trade partners.

Speaking at the webinar, High Commissioner of Maldives to Singapore, H.E. Ibrahim Shaheeb reiterated that Singapore is an important contributor with huge potential for Maldives economic recovery, and noted that increasing tourist arrivals has been a key priority of the government since the setback from the COVID 19. Also speaking at the webinar were Managing Director Mr. Thoyyib Mohamed of Maldives Marketing & PR Corporation, Deputy Minister, Dr. Naushad Mohamed from Ministry of Tourism, and the President of Guest House Association of Maldives, Mr. Abdulla Nasheed.

In her concluding remarks, Deputy High Commissioner Ms. Eman Hussain noted that the webinar is a useful first step towards enhancing B2B relations between Singapore travel agents and Maldives partners, and thanked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other government agencies, as well as NATAS and Maldives tourism industry partners for their productive participation in the webinar. She said that the Maldives looks forward to welcoming Singapore back to the sunny side of life soon.

The webinar supports Government’s continued efforts to build a stronger, more sustainable and resilient tourism economy and to do so in coordination with close partners.

en.title: The Permanent Representative of Maldives to the International Renewable Energy Agency presents credentials to the Director General of the International Renewable Energy Agency
en.description: The Permanent Representative of Maldives to the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) presents credentials to the Director General of IRENA
en.body:
The Permanent Representative of Maldives to the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) presents credentials to the Director General of IRENA

The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), Ambassador Aminath Shabeena, today presented her Letter of Credence to the Director-General of IRENA, Mr. Francesco La Camera in an official ceremony held at the Headquarters of IRENA in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Ambassador Shabeena succeeds High Commissioner Dr. Hussain Niyaaz to become the second Permanent Representative of Maldives to IRENA. She was officially designated as the Permanent Representative of Maldives to IRENA on 31 March 2021.

At the ceremony, Ambassador Shabeena thanked Director-General Mr. Francesco La Camera for the assistance provided by IRENA to the Maldives to date, and conveyed compliments from President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid. She reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Maldives in working towards transitioning to sustainable energy forms and reassured to further strengthen cooperation with IRENA to help the Maldives achieve its Nationally Determined Contribution of reaching net-zero emissions by 2030.

The International Renewable Energy Agency is an intergovernmental organization that was officially established in 2009. At present, IRENA comprises of 164 Member States. The Maldives has been an active member of IRENA since its formation, including in the capacity of Vice Chair of the Assembly of IRENA, following the elections in 2013. In October 2017, the inaugural meeting of the Renewable Island Energy (IRIE) was also held in the Maldives.

During the virtual meeting, both Minister Shahid and Administrator Power discussed the on-going COVID-19 pandemic in the two countries and the ongoing areas of cooperation especially in the areas of protecting the environment, strengthening democratic governance and public finance management in the Maldives. Minister Shahid also thanked the Government of the United States for their continued assistance to the Maldives, and commended the US Government’s recent announcement to include Maldives among the first countries that would receive the extra stocks of COVID-19 vaccines from the US. Minister Shahid also noted that the United States have proven to be a close and reliable friend, especially at times of critical need.

The Government of the United States has provided over USD 20 million in assistance to the Maldives since 2001, including over USD 9.1 million in assistance provided to the Maldives to assist in COVID-19 relief and recovery efforts. USAID has also made generous donations in the recent past including critical care ventilators and multiple batches of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and medical equipment to the Maldives to help better combat the pandemic.
