en.title: Embassy of Maldives in Tokyo hosts ‘Exclusive Webinar on Maldives Tourism in Post-Covid Recovery’
en.description: Embassy of Maldives in Tokyo hosts ‘Exclusive Webinar on Maldives Tourism in Post-Covid Recovery’
en.body:
Embassy of Maldives in Tokyo hosts ‘Exclusive Webinar on Maldives Tourism in Post-Covid Recovery’

Embassy of the Maldives in Japan hosted a webinar entitled “Exclusive Webinar on Maldives Tourism in Post-Covid Recovery” today in coordination with Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Tourism, Maldives Marketing & PR Corporation, Guest House Association of Maldives.

The Government agencies provided an overview of efforts underway to recover rebuild and restore tourism sector post-pandemic. With participation of 23 major Japanese Travel Agents and Tour Operators, which covers 80% of the Japanese Market for Maldives tourism, the webinar provided an important forum to prepare for the anticipated increase of tourist arrivals from Japan in the coming months. The webinar also supports the government’s continued initiatives to strengthen tourism sector and provided information to travel agents about existing guidelines and practices for international tourists in the Maldives.

Managing Director Mr. Thoyyib Mohamed of Maldives Marketing & PR Corporation, Deputy Minister, Dr. Naushad Mohamed from Ministry of Tourism, and the President of Guest House Association of Maldives, Mr. Abdulla Nasheed spoke at the event and interacted with the participants through a live Q&A session.

Speaking at the event was also H.E. Ibrahim Uvais, Ambassador of Maldives to Japan, who highlighted the importance of the event in Maldives efforts to rebuild and recover from COVID-19. The Ambassador also thanked the Government of Japan for its continued assistance and support to the Maldives in its effort to build back better post COVID-19. Today’s event marks as the first of the series of ‘Maldives Business Seminars’ scheduled to be organized by the Embassy of Japan in Maldives for the year.

en.title: Non-Resident High Commissioner of Maldives to Seychelles presents Credentials to the President of Seychelles
en.description: Non-Resident High Commissioner of Maldives to Seychelles presents Credentials to the President of Seychelles
en.body:
Non-Resident High Commissioner of Maldives to Seychelles presents Credentials to the President of Seychelles

The Non-Resident High Commissioner Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Maldives to the Republic of Seychelles, Omar Abdul Razzak, presented his Letter of Credence to the President of the Republic of Seychelles, Wavel Ramkalawan, at a ceremony held at the State House in Victoria this morning.

During the courtesy call following the ceremony, President Ramkalawan congratulated the High Commissioner on the commencement of his term, and conveyed greetings to President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of Maldives. President Ramkalawan also reaffirmed commitment of the Government of Seychelles to enhance the blossoming relations between the two countries and stated the confidence that the bilateral relations will reach new heights with the appointment of the first Non-Resident High Commissioner of Maldives to Seychelles.

High Commissioner Razzak expressed his gratitude for being given the honour to present his Letter of Credence, and serve as the first Non-Resident High Commissioner of Maldives to Seychelles. High Commissioner Razzak further expressed his commitment to work closely with Seychelles Government with a renewed focus in enhancing the bilateral relations in areas of mutual interest including, promoting trade, investments, culture and tourism between the two countries.

The ceremony was attended by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Tourism of Seychelles, Sylvestre Radegonde, the Principal Secretary for Foreign Affairs, Vivianne Fock Tave, Honorary Consul of the Republic of Maldives in Seychelles, Lambert Bonne and officials of the Department of Foreign Affairs of Seychelles. The High Commissioner was accompanied to the ceremony by the Third Secretary of the High Commission of Maldives in Colombo, Sri Lanka, Aishath Nihad.

High Commissioner Razzak also paid courtesy calls on the Vice President of Seychelles, Ahmed Afif and several members of the Cabinet after the ceremony. High Commissioner Razzak is also scheduled to pay courtesy calls on the Speaker of National Assembly of Seychelles and other Cabinet Ministers during the visit.

en.title: The 47th Session of the Human Rights Council to begins in Geneva
en.description: The 47th Session of the Human Rights Council to begins in Geneva
en.body:
The 47th Session of the Human Rights Council to begins in Geneva

The 47th Session of the Human Rights Council commenced in Geneva this morning. This hybrid session will continue for four weeks, from 21 June to 13 July 2021. A delegation from the Maldives will constructively engage in the session, through Interactive Dialogues, Panel Discussions and discussions on key resolutions.

The Maldives, as the Co-chair and on behalf of the “Informal Group of SIDS” along with Haiti, will also lead a cross regional Joint Statement under the Panel Discussion on Climate Change, and State Response to Pandemics. The Maldives, as part of the Core Group on Freedom of Assembly and Association, with other members consisting of Indonesia, Lithuania, Mexico, United States of America and the Czech Republic will be leading a Joint Statement on Freedom of Assembly. The Maldives will also be hosting a side event with Costa Rica, Slovenia, Switzerland and Morocco, on the legal aspects of the Right to a Clean, Safe, Healthy and Sustainable Environment.

The Maldives, as part of Regional and political Groups including the OIC and the Non-Aligned Movement, has shared concerns on the human rights violations that are escalating around the world and will address some of these concerns, as part of its work to promote and protect human rights for all. In this regard, the Maldives will deliver statements among others, on the issue of the human rights situation in Palestine and on the Rohingya Muslim minorities in Myanmar.

The priorities of the Maldives at the UN Human Rights Council include women’s rights, climate change and environment, and civil and political rights. The Maldives will actively engage in the negotiations and co-sponsor several resolutions in these areas. Some of the key resolutions for the Maldives at this session are: violence against women, climate change and human rights, and trafficking in persons.

The Maldives' delegation will be led by His Excellency Dr. Asim Ahmed, Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Office at Geneva and other International Organizations. The delegation also includes Ms. Hawla Ahmed Didi, Deputy Permanent Representative of Maldives to United Nations Office at Geneva, Ms. Shahiya Ali Manik, First Secretary, Permanent Mission of Maldives to United Nations Office at Geneva and Mr. Adam Hamid, Director, Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The Maldives has served as a Member of the Human Rights Council for 2 conservative terms of 6 years, from 2011 to 2016. Maldives is currently an Observer State of the Council. Maldives has also presented its candidature to the Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025, for which the elections will take place in June 2022, in New York. The Human Rights Council is an inter-governmental body within the United Nations system, made up of 47 Member States who hold the responsibility for strengthening the promotion and protection of human rights throughout the world.

en.title: Minister Shahid meets the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of UAE
en.description: Minister Shahid meets the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of UAE
en.body:
Minister Shahid meets the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of UAE

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the United Arab Emirates, His Highness Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, in Abu Dhabi, today.

During the meeting, both Ministers shared the recent updates on the situation of the Covid-19 pandemic in their respective countries, and elaborated on strategies to recover from the effects of the pandemic and build back stronger and more resilient. Minister Shahid reiterated gratitude for the generous Covid-19 related assistance given to the Maldives by UAE.

The two Ministers also reflected on the increased level of cooperation between the Maldives and UAE in recent years, and reaffirmed the commitment towards sustaining the close bond.

Minister Shahid reflected on the developmental projects underway in the Maldives and conveyed appreciation, on behalf of the Government of Maldives, for the constant support provided by the Government of UAE, towards the attainment of the Maldives’ socio-economic development goals.

Minister Shahid and Minister Al Nahyan reaffirmed their commitment to foster the strong spirit of cooperation between the Maldives and UAE, bilaterally and multilaterally, and continue to work closely together on issues of mutual interest.

The meeting was attended by Ambassador of Maldives to United Arab Emirates, Aminath Shabeena and the Director of West Asia Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the United Arab Emirates, Khalid Alamri.

en.title: Minister Shahid meets with the Director General of Abu Dhabi Fund for Development
en.description: Minister Shahid meets with the Director General of Abu Dhabi Fund for Development
en.body:
Minister Shahid meets with the Director General of Abu Dhabi Fund for Development

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, met with the Director General of Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD), Mohammed Saif Al Suwaidi, in Dubai.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid and Director General Al Suwaidi reflected on the long-standing bond between the Maldives and UAE as close friends and partners. Minister Shahid and Director General Al Suwaidi discussed the key ongoing projects in the Maldives, which are being carried out with the generous assistance of UAE, and explored ways to finalize and move forward with pipeline projects.

Minister Shahid highlighted that one of the most notable ventures by ADFD in the Maldives during recent years was the successful completion of the first phase of Maafaru International Airport, in Noonu Atoll, which has yielded immense benefits for the region, and introduced new prospects for many Maldivians. Minister Shahid expressed confidence that the second phase of the project, including further development of the airport, in collaboration with ADFD, would result in the realization of even more opportunities.

Minister Shahid reiterated gratitude on behalf of the Government of Maldives for the invaluable role played by ADFD, in supporting the development journey of the Maldives. Director General Al Suwaidi assured Minister Shahid of the commitment of ADFD to continue to extend support as a development partner of the Maldives.

en.title: Maldives participates in the Eleventh Bi-Annual Meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials of IORA
en.description: Maldives participates in the Eleventh Bi-Annual Meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials of IORA
en.body:
Maldives participates in the Eleventh Bi-Annual Meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials of IORA

A delegation from the Republic of Maldives participated in the Eleventh Bi-Annual Meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), which took place virtually from 15-16 June 2021. The meeting was attended by the 23 Member States of IORA, the Acting Secretary General and 10 Specialized Agencies.

The Bi-Annual Meeting took note of the progress made since December 2020 under the six priority areas and two cross-cutting areas of the Association. The six priority areas of IORA are: Maritime Safety and Security; Trade and Investment Facilitation; Fisheries Management; Disaster Risk Management; Academic and Scientific Cooperation; and Tourism Promotion and Cultural Exchanges. The two cross-cutting areas are: Women’s Economic Empowerment and Blue Economy.

The Member States also provided updates on the preparations for forthcoming events and meetings of IORA’s institutional mechanisms, as well as IORA’s engagement with its Dialogue Partners, International partners and special programmes, considering the ongoing impact of COVID-19.

The meeting of the IORA’s Sub-Committee on Finance was held on 9 June 2021 in the lead up to the meeting. The Sub-Committee discussed issues related to Good Governance and Financial Management of the IORA Secretariat.

The Meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials was chaired by H.E. Abdulnasser Alshaali, Assistant Minister for Economic and Trade Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, UAE. UAE assumed the position of Chair of IORA in November 2019, with the theme, “Promoting a Shared Destiny and Path to Prosperity in the Indian Ocean”.

The Maldives delegation was led by His Excellency Ahmed Shiaan, Additional Secretary, accompanied by Ms. Mariyam Reesha, Director General and Ms. Fathmath Lamya Imthiyaz, Desk Officer of the Ministry.

IORA is an intergovernmental regional organization providing a forum for member states and dialogue partners to enhance socio-economic cooperation. Maldives joined the IORA in 2019 as its 22nd Member State.

“On behalf of the Government and the People of the Maldives, and on my own behalf, it is my pleasure to convey sincere felicitations and warm greetings to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of the Russian Federation, on the momentous occasion of Russia Day.
